title: Deep-Learning Solution Providing Molecular Marker Subtyping of Breast Cancer Whole Slide Images: Protocol for a UK Clinical Service Evaluation Study.
authors: Walsh, Elizabeth; Rathore, Dildar; Geraldes, Andre; Arslan, Salim; Hanby, Andrew M; Millican-Slater, Rebecca; Drummond, Michael; Rotimi, Olorunda; Kumar, Narender; Pandya, Pahini; Orsi, Nicolas M
one_liner_zh: 该文是乳腺癌全切片图像深度学习分子分型临床评估方案，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: As the histopathology workforce continues to struggle and service demand continues to increase, it has become prudent to consider viable avenues to try to alleviate diagnostic workload burden. One such avenue is computer-based technologies (CBTs). Breast cancer (BC) is the most common malignant neoplasm in the United Kingdom and requires additional testing for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (HER2) status at the time of histological diagnosis. This makes BC diagnostics a promising candidate for the application of an efficient CBT. However, for clinical acceptance, these technologies must prove that they work within a real-life diagnostic environment. OBJECTIVE: We present a study protocol for a prospective clinical service evaluation aimed to validate a UK Conformity Assessed-marked CBT's ability to provide ER, PR, and HER2 results for invasive BCs from scanned hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole slide images. METHODS: This protocol has been designed to use and mimic a preexisting digital pathology workflow within a National Health Service tertiary referral cancer center without disrupting normal patient care. Eligible cases are identified prospectively through the laboratory information management system, and their whole slide images are extracted from the clinical digital workflow. After verification of national data opt-out status and the exclusion of appropriate cases (N=400 analyzable cases), these cases are analyzed on a dedicated computer in parallel to the existing clinical workflow by a UK Conformity Assessed-marked deep learning-based CBT in a separate environment, providing results for ER, PR, and HER2 status. These results are compared to the ER, PR, and HER2 status reported on the corresponding pathology report. To evaluate the CBT's performance, a range of accepted concordance measures will be applied, including specificity, sensitivity, false-positive rate, false-negative rate, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value. Moreover, time stamps representing the duration of image analysis will also be collected. RESULTS: This study started in April 2025. There are no results to present, as this paper focuses on study design, and results have yet to be generated. As of March 2026, overall, 366 potentially analyzable cases have been collected. The anticipated end date of the study is May 2026 (400-case target). Results will be presented in a separate publication. CONCLUSIONS: This design assesses a CBT within a clinical environment while effectively eliminating any unwanted effects on patient care. This type of service evaluation provides a useful step to establish confidence in a CBT before trialing its effect on patient care. It also offers the opportunity to support interventional randomized controlled trials, health economic evaluations, and usability studies. This protocol will hopefully prove useful to others who wish to conduct a similar service evaluation at their own institution. INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/76785.
abstract_zh: 背景：随着组织病理学劳动力持续紧张，服务需求不断增加，考虑可行的途径以减轻诊断工作负担已变得审慎。其中一条途径是基于计算机的技术（CBTs）。乳腺癌（BC）是英国最常见的恶性肿瘤，在组织学诊断时需要对雌激素受体（ER）、孕激素受体（PR）和人表皮生长因子受体-2（HER2）状态进行额外检测。这使得乳腺癌诊断成为应用高效CBT的有前景的候选领域。然而，为了获得临床接受，这些技术必须证明其在真实诊断环境中有效。目的：我们提出一项前瞻性临床服务评估的研究方案，旨在验证一款英国符合性评估标记的CBT，其能够从扫描的苏木精-伊红染色全切片图像中提供浸润性乳腺癌的ER、PR和HER2结果。方法：本方案设计用于使用并模拟国家卫生服务三级转诊癌症中心内已有的数字病理工作流程，且不干扰正常患者护理。符合条件的病例通过实验室信息管理系统前瞻性识别，其全切片图像从临床数字工作流程中提取。在验证国家数据选择退出状态并排除适当病例后（N=400例可分析病例），这些病例在专用计算机上，与现有临床工作流程并行，在独立环境中由一款英国符合性评估标记的基于深度学习的CBT进行分析，提供ER、PR和HER2状态结果。这些结果与相应病理报告中报告的ER、PR和HER2状态进行比较。为评估CBT的性能，将应用一系列公认的一致性指标，包括特异性、敏感性、假阳性率、假阴性率、阳性预测值和阴性预测值。此外，还将收集代表图像分析持续时间的时戳。结果：本研究于2025年4月开始。目前尚无结果可呈现，因为本文侧重于研究设计，结果尚未生成。截至2026年3月，共收集了366例潜在可分析病例。研究的预计结束日期为2026年5月（目标400例）。结果将在单独出版物中呈现。结论：本设计在临床环境中评估CBT，同时有效消除对患者护理的任何不良影响。这种类型的服务评估为在试验CBT对患者护理影响之前建立信心提供了有用步骤。它还提供了支持干预性随机对照试验、卫生经济学评估和可用性研究的机会。本方案有望对希望在自己机构进行类似服务评估的其他人有用。国际注册报告标识符（IRRID）：DERR1-10.2196/76785。
